desc:
A ramp in nums is a pair of indices (i, j) with i < j and nums[i] ≤ nums[j]. Its width is j - i.

Return the largest width of any ramp, or 0 if there is no ramp at all.

Example: nums = [6, 0, 8, 2, 1, 5] returns 4, using i = 1 (value 0) and j = 5 (value 5).
hints: Trying every pair is O(n<sup>2</sup>). For a fixed right end j, which left ends i are even worth considering?
A left end i is useless if some earlier index has a value that is smaller or equal: that earlier index gives a wider ramp for every j. So only strict prefix minima can be the best left end.

Collect the indices of strict prefix minima (their values decrease). Then scan j from the right; while the top candidate has a value ≤ nums[j], pop it and record the width. Popped candidates are never needed again, because a smaller j gives a smaller width.
editorial: The best left end is always a position where the prefix minimum drops to a new strict low: if an earlier index k has nums[k] ≤ nums[i], then any ramp starting at i can start at k instead and be wider. List those indices left to right; their values are strictly decreasing.

Now sweep j from the right end to the left. The top of the candidate list is the candidate with the largest index and the smallest value. While it satisfies nums[cand] ≤ nums[j], it forms a ramp with j; record j - cand and discard it. It can be discarded safely: every later j is smaller, so it can only give narrower ramps with this candidate.
Each index enters and leaves the candidate list at most once, so the work is O(n) time and O(n) space. A binary search over the candidate list per j gives O(n log n) and is also acceptable.
